en.title: What a Syllable Is
en.summary: Every syllable in Romanian builds around exactly one clear vowel sound.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: In Romanian, every beat of a word is a syllable. Each syllable has one vowel sound at its center. This vowel gives the syllable its loud voice. Listen to (mama) /ˈma.ma/, which means mother. You hear two beats. Each beat holds one vowel.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Open your mouth for each vowel. Do not rush through the vowel sound. In (mama) /ˈma.ma/, your voice stresses the first beat. Your pitch rises a little on that first beat. Then, your mouth makes the second beat softly. Keep both vowel sounds clear and steady.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Count the vowel letters to find the syllables. One vowel sound makes one syllable. Look at (apă) /ˈa.pə/, which means water. It has two vowel sounds and two syllables. Consonants attach to the vowel. The vowel is always the main heart of each syllable.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not drop the vowel sound at the end of a word. Every syllable needs its vowel. Do not swallow vowels or blur them together. In (casă) /ˈka.sə/, which means house, say both beats fully. Give each syllable its own distinct, open sound.
